facts.text: The vaulted ceiling of the I Carracci restaurant is entirely frescoed by the school of the Carracci brothers.

facts.text: The hotel's historic wine cellar is known today as Enoteca Morandi, in homage to the Bolognese painter Giorgio Morandi.
facts.excerpt: The historic wine cellar of the Grand Hotel Majestic “già Baglioni”, it is known today as Enoteca Morandi, in homage to one of the most important Bolognese painters of the 20th century, Giorgio Morandi.

facts.text: The Enoteca Wine Bar hosts wine and food tastings with the hotel's sommelier.

facts.text: The Terrazza Torre and Terrazza Foyer terraces are on the piano nobile, reserved for the suites; the Terrazza Torre overlooks Palazzo Fava.
facts.excerpt: Located on the piano nobile, reserved for the suites, the Terrazza Torre - overlooking Palazzo Fava - and the Terrazza Foyer offer an intimate and discreet atmosphere.

facts.text: The terraces can be booked for drinks or light snacks, with a fee for the dedicated service.
facts.excerpt: The terraces can be booked for drinks or light snacks, with a fee for the dedicated service.

facts.text: The Café Marinetti floor was made by Tuscan artisans in Art Deco style using Statuario, Nero Marquinia and Giallo Siena marbles from Carrara.
facts.excerpt: The flooring, a genuine work of art, was made by Tuscan artisans in Art Deco style, using precious Statuario, Nero Marquinia and Giallo Siena marbles from Carrara.

facts.text: The breakfast room opens onto the original winter garden, with early-1900s trompe-l'oeil paintings and a solarium roof that can be opened in the warmer months.
